title: Activation links replace temp passwords for invite and reset
context: The initial admin invite/reset flow returned a temp password in the response payload. That has three problems: (a) the admin sees and holds a working credential, (b) the temp password sits in browser and server logs, (c) there's no expiry — a leaked temp password stays valid forever. Every enterprise treasury tool the research covered handles this as an activation link.
decision: Introduce single-use, 24-hour activation links. Invite and reset both issue a token via the new `activation_service`. The raw token is shown to the admin exactly once (they share it out of band); only its SHA-256 hash is stored. The invitee visits `/activate?token=…`, sets their own password, and the token is marked consumed. Neither the admin nor Treasury Register ever sees the chosen password.

shape.table: activation_token { id, tenant_id, user_id, token_hash (sha256), purpose IN('INVITE','RESET'), expires_at, consumed_at, created_by, created_at }
public_endpoints: GET /api/v1/activate/{token} — non-consuming lookup; shows email + display_name + purpose
POST /api/v1/activate — consume the token, set password, return a bearer token (auto sign-in)
admin_endpoints_changed: POST /admin/users — invite; response now { user, activation_url, expires_at, note } instead of { user, temp_password, note }
POST /admin/users/{id}/reset-password — response now { user_id, activation_url, expires_at }; breaks the existing password immediately
shape.sentinel_password_hash: activation_service.UNUSABLE_PASSWORD_HASH = '!pending-activation' — verify_password against it always returns False, so an invited user exists (can hold roles + scope) but cannot sign in until they consume the activation token.

invariants: The raw token is shown to the admin exactly once, in the API response. Never stored, never logged in full (only a token-prefix goes to the console for debugging).
Only the SHA-256 of the token is persisted; the token cannot be recovered from the DB.
Tokens are single-use — consumption marks consumed_at.
Issuing a new token for a user revokes any live unconsumed tokens for that user (one active activation link at a time).
Reset breaks the existing password immediately — the previous credentials stop working the second the admin clicks Reset, not when the invitee opens the link.
audit_trail: user.invited audit event carries { email, roles, expires_at }
Successful sign-in via consumed token writes user.signed_in as normal (IdentityService.sign_in path)

frontend.new_route: /activate?token=… — public, unauthenticated page. Resolves the token, shows welcome + password form, consumes on submit, signs the user in via startSession(), redirects to /
admin_ui: InviteModal shows ActivationLinkCard with the full URL (window.location.origin + activation_url) + copy button + expiry
EditUserPanel Reset password shows the same ActivationLinkCard for a RESET-purpose token
Users table adds a 'Pending activation' badge next to Status when the user has a live unconsumed token

future_work: SMTP: send activation emails so the admin doesn't have to share the link manually. Log-to-console + copy-from-UI is the prototype default; production wires an SMTP/SendGrid/SES adapter behind activation_service.issue_token.
Rate limiting: no abuse controls yet on POST /activate. Anonymous endpoints should get IP-based throttling before this ships beyond a demo.
Password policy: 8-char minimum is a placeholder; real policy (length, complexity, breached-password check via HaveIBeenPwned) belongs in system_policy.
